version.changelog: Add Phase 0: pre-recording discipline - write task requirements and plan to daily notes before execution to survive crashes without losing context. Also includes post-task cleanup of working memory.

llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions align with its stated purpose (orchestrating large/multi-step tasks); it writes local checkpoint files and suggests running helper scripts, and it does not request unexpected credentials or network installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (complex task orchestration) matches the SKILL.md and the included checkpoint utility. The script and docs focus on checkpointing, splitting work, sub-agent orchestration, and file-based WAL—functions appropriate for an orchestrator.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions direct the agent to write logs/checkpoints (e.g., memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md, ~/.openclaw/workspace/checkpoints), to prefer file-based result passing for sub-agents, and to create/run helper Python scripts (exec). This is in-scope for an orchestrator, but it grants the agent discretion to create and execute scripts and to read/write files in the user's home directory; users should be aware that executing arbitrary scripts can run arbitrary code.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only with a small helper script. Nothing is downloaded or extracted from remote URLs and no packages are installed by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The docs reference external services (Feishu API, EC2 resource limits) but do not request associated tokens; that is reasonable — those credentials would be provided by the user when actually integrating with external APIs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true. The skill writes checkpoint files into ~/.openclaw/workspace/checkpoints (its own data area) but does not modify other skills or request permanent platform privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for orchestrating large multi-step or batch tasks: it records WAL-style checkpoints and recommends safe sub-agent patterns. Before installing, review and accept these points: (1) the skill will create/read files under your home directory (~/.openclaw/workspace/checkpoints and other paths referenced) — ensure you’re comfortable with that location; (2) the docs recommend creating and exec-ing Python scripts to process data — only run trusted code and consider sandboxing or reviewing generated scripts before execution; (3) integrations mentioned (Feishu, EC2) require external API tokens or libs which the skill does not request — supply them separately and avoid putting secrets in global envs the skill can access if you don’t want the agent to use them; (4) the skill's advice to write files instead of relying on announce/messages is appropriate, but monitor disk usage if you run many large tasks. If you want higher assurance, request the author to (a) explicitly document all file paths used, (b) avoid auto-exec of scripts or require explicit user confirmation for exec, and (c) confirm there are no hidden network calls — additional source code beyond the provided files would change the assessment.
